title: Equal parts in a regular bipartite graph
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $k \ge 1$ be a positive integer such that every vertex of $G$ has degree exactly $k$. Suppose that $G$ is bipartite with parts $s$ and $t$; that is, $s$ and $t$ are disjoint sets of vertices whose union contains every vertex, and every edge of $G$ joins a vertex of $s$ to a vertex of $t$. Then the two parts have the same size, $\abs{s} = \abs{t}$.
hypotheses_covered: k is a positive integer (0 < k)
G is k-regular (every vertex has degree k)
G is bipartite with parts s and t
replaced:
\emph{If a \texttt{k}-regular bipartite graph with \texttt{k > 0} has
bipartition \texttt{(X, Y)}, then \texttt{|X| = |Y|}.}
